question: What is AIT?
gold_answer:
The Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), founded in 1959, is a not-for-profit international English-speaking postgraduate institution located on a green campus north of Bangkok, Thailand.

AIT offers the opportunity to study at an institution in Asia which possesses a global reputation. Going forward, AIT will be stressing its global connections, injection of innovation into research and teaching, its relevance to industry, and its nurturing of entrepreneurship, while continuing to fulfill its social impact and capacity building role. Sitting on a beautiful green campus located just north of Bangkok, Thailand, AIT operates as a multicultural community where a cosmopolitan approach to living and learning is the rule. You will meet and study with people from all around the world.

Today, AIT’s internationally recognized engineering, environment, and management graduates are highly sought after by employers in their home countryand elsewhere. Across many walks of life in Asia, AIT alumni have distinguished themselves as CEO’s of private and state enterprises, as business owners, as well-respected researchers and faculty, and as senior university and government officials.

question: What is AIT’s mission and vision?
gold_answer:
AIT (Asian Institute of Technology) aims to be a leading graduate institution for Asia's sustainable development, fostering future leaders through relevant education, research, and problem-solving in technology, engineering, and management, by connecting with industry and promoting innovation for real-world impact. Its mission focuses on developing highly qualified professionals and delivering knowledge to tackle regional and global challenges, while its vision emphasizes regional integration, leadership in advanced education, and impactful solutions for a sustainable future. 
AIT's Vision:
To be a globally recognized leader in advanced education and research, driving sustainable development in Asia.
To be an exemplary institution that integrates the region into the global economy through innovation and partnership. 
AIT's Mission:
To develop future-focused, problem-solving professionals through rigorous education, leveraging diverse expertise.
To provide need-responsive, high-quality education and training in technology, engineering, management, and sustainability.
To generate impactful solutions to societal and industry challenges by applying research and knowledge.
To build strong connections with industry and community partners for knowledge transfer and sustainable development.

question: What academic programs and courses does AIT offer?
gold_answer:
The Asian Institute of Technology (AIT) offers a wide range of graduate-level academic programs and courses, primarily at the Master’s and Doctoral (PhD) levels. These programs are designed to address regional and global challenges through advanced education, research, and practical application.

Academic Programs at AIT

AIT’s programs are organized under three main schools, each offering multiple fields of study:

1. School of Engineering and Technology (SET)

Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Computer Science

Information and Communications Technologies

Civil and Infrastructure Engineering

Environmental Engineering and Management

Electrical and Electronic Engineering

Mechanical, Industrial, and Manufacturing Engineering

2. School of Management (SOM)

Business Administration (MBA)

Management of Technology

International Business

Finance

Marketing

Entrepreneurship and Innovation

3. School of Environment, Resources and Development (SERD)

Sustainable Development

Environmental Management

Energy and Climate Change

Agricultural Systems and Engineering

Urban Environmental Management

Courses and Study Structure

Programs typically include core courses, electives, and either a thesis, research project, or capstone.

Courses are taught in English.

Both research-oriented and coursework-based options are available, depending on the program.

Some programs are interdisciplinary, drawing courses from multiple schools.

Additional Academic Offerings

Doctoral (PhD) programs with strong research focus

Short courses, professional training, and executive education (program-dependent)

question: Which schools or faculties at AIT offer each academic program?
gold_answer:
Academic Programs and Their Schools at AIT
School of Engineering and Technology (SET)

Offers engineering, technology, and related programs, including:

Departments and Programs:

Department of Civil and Infrastructure Engineering

Construction, Engineering and Infrastructure Management

Geotechnical and Earth Resources Engineering

Structural Engineering

Transportation Engineering

Water Engineering and Management

Department of Industrial Systems Engineering

Bio-Nano Material Science and Engineering

Mechatronics and Machine Intelligence

Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering

Medical Engineering

Department of Information and Communication Technologies

Computer Science

Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Information & Communications Technologies

Information Management

Internet of Things (IoT) Systems Engineering

Remote Sensing and Geographic Information Systems

Telecommunications
(Source: Official AIT program pages)

Additionally, SET also offers Professional Master’s programs in technical and engineering specialties, such as professional data science, construction, and geotechnical engineering.

School of Environment, Resources and Development (SERD)

Focuses on sustainable development, environment, agriculture, and energy programs:

Departments and Programs:

Department of Food, Agriculture and Natural Resources

AgriBusiness Management

Agricultural Systems & Engineering

Aquaculture and Aquatic Resources Management

Food Engineering and Bioprocess Technology

Food Innovation, Nutrition and Health

Natural Resources Management

Department of Energy and Climate Change

Climate Change and Sustainable Development

Sustainable Energy Transition

Department of Development and Sustainability

Development and Sustainability

Development Planning Management and Innovation

Gender and Development Studies

Urban Innovation and Sustainability
(Source: Official AIT program pages)

SERD also participates in inter-school programs jointly offered with other schools.

School of Management (SOM)

Focuses on business, management, and related fields:

Programs:

Master of Business Administration (MBA)

Business Analytics and Digital Transformation (MSc)

International Finance (MSc)

Digital Marketing (MSc)

Environmental, Social and Governance (Professional Master)
(These offerings reflect the main management programs; curricula may vary by term.)

SOM also offers professional and executive programs in finance, banking, and entrepreneurship.

Joint / Inter-School Academic Programs

Some programs combine expertise from multiple schools:

Disaster Preparedness, Mitigation, and Management (SET + SERD)

Urban Water Engineering & Management (SET + SERD)

Water Security and Global Change (SET + SERD)

Social Business and Entrepreneurship (SERD + SOM)
(Source: Various listings including combined program sections)

Doctoral Programs

Doctoral (PhD and DBA) programs are also offered through the same schools:

SET: Advanced engineering and technology research fields

SERD: Environment, development, and sustainability research

SOM: Business and management research (PhD / DBA)
(Source: archived doctoral listings)

question: Are AIT programs offered on a full-time or part-time basis?
gold_answer:
At the Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), academic programs are offered primarily on a full-time basis.

Key details

Most Master’s and Doctoral programs are full-time, with on-campus study required.

Programs are designed to be academically intensive, combining coursework, research, and/or thesis work that requires regular campus engagement.

Part-time study is generally not available for regular academic degree programs.

Some professional, executive, or short-term programs may offer more flexible formats, but these are exceptions and are program-specific.

Practical implication

Applicants should plan for full-time enrollment and residence in Thailand for the duration of their studies, especially for visa and academic requirements.

For confirmation on any program-specific flexibility, applicants should check the official program page or consult AIT Admissions, as availability may vary by program and intake.

question: What are the requirements to apply to AIT?
gold_answer:
Academic Requirements
Master's Programs: A Bachelor's degree from a recognized university, usually with a GPA of at least 2.75 (or equivalent) on a 4.0 scale. Some programs may have higher GPA requirements or require a degree in a specific field.
Doctoral Programs: A Master's degree from a recognized university, with a strong academic record (typically a GPA of 3.50 or above on a 4.0 scale). Evidence of research ability, often in the form of a Master's thesis, is usually required.
English Language Proficiency
Since English is the official language of instruction at AIT, applicants must demonstrate a certain level of English proficiency. This is typically done by submitting a satisfactory score from one of the following standardized tests:
IELTS: A minimum score of 6.0 (with no band score below 5.5) is generally required for Master's programs.
TOEFL: Internet-based (iBT): A score of 80 or higher.
Paper-based: A score of 550 or higher.
AIT's own English Entry Test: The institute also offers its own test for applicants who are unable to take the IELTS or TOEFL.
Required Application Documents
When applying, you will generally need to prepare the following documents:
Completed Application Form: This is usually submitted online through the AIT admissions portal.
Official Transcripts and Degree Certificates: You will need to provide certified copies of your academic records from all universities previously attended.
Two Letters of Recommendation: These should be from professors or employers who are familiar with your academic and/or professional abilities.
Statement of Purpose: A written essay detailing your academic and career goals, and why you are interested in the specific program at AIT.
Proof of English Language Proficiency: Your official IELTS, TOEFL, or AIT test score report.
Copy of your Passport
Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume

- If you're applying for the **Flexible Master’s Option**, you still need to **select a program** (not a specific major) when applying.
- You can choose from a list of **selected programs** that are available under the Flexible Master’s Option.

- Some programs allow you to **choose specializations or majors** after admission.
- For example, in the **Master of Science in Engineering**, you may choose to specialize in **Mechanical Engineering**, **Electrical Engineering**, or **Civil Engineering**.
- In other programs, such as the **Master of Business Administration (MBA)**, you may choose a **specialization** like **Finance**, **Marketing**, or **Human Resources**.

- During the **application process**, you will be asked to **select a program**.
- You may not be required to choose a **specific major** at this stage.
- After admission, you may be given the opportunity to **select your major or specializations** based on the program's structure.

- If you're applying for the **Flexible Master’s Option**, you can **attend classes online** or **on campus**.
- You can **choose to study from home** or **come to campus** as needed.
- You can **pay course-by-course** and **enroll in a minimum of 6 credits per semester**.

question: What is the minimum EET score required?
gold_answer: Minimum Score is 6
generated_answer:
The English proficiency requirements for admission to AIT's programs are standardized across most master's and professional master's programs. Here's a consolidated overview based on the provided sources:

### **English Proficiency Requirements**
1. **AIT English Entrance Test (EET):**  
   - Minimum score: **6.0** (Writing band only).  
   - This is AIT's own English proficiency test, equivalent to other standardized tests.

2. **IELTS (Academic):**  
   - Minimum score: **6.0** (Overall band score).  
   - **Writing band requirement:** 6.0.  

3. **TOEFL (iBT):**  
   - Minimum score: **80** (Overall score).  
   - **Writing section requirement:** 21–23.  

4. **TOEFL (CBT):**  
   - Minimum score: **213** (Overall score).  
   - **Writing section requirement:** 25–26.  

5. **TOEFL (Paper-Based):**  
   - Minimum score: **550** (Overall score).  
   - **Writing section requirement:** 59–61.  

---

### **Key Notes**
- **All programs** (e.g., M-MSc-IF, PMESG, PME-GEM, PMB&F) require **one of the above English proficiency tests** to meet the minimum threshold.  
- **Writing band scores** are critical for all tests, as they directly correlate with the required English proficiency level.  
- **AIT-EET** is the institution-specific test, and applicants must achieve a **6.0** in the writing section to qualify.  

---

### **Additional Context**
- **Minimum GPA Requirement:**  
  - For most programs, a **minimum GPA of 2.75** (or equivalent) is required for admission.  
  - This is separate from the English proficiency requirements.  

- **Program-Specific Notes:**  
  - **Professional Master’s Programs (e.g., PMESG, PME-GEM):**  
    - Require **at least 3 years of work experience** in relevant fields.  
    - Delivery modes include **on-campus** (Vietnam campus) or **hybrid** (online/in-person).  
  - **Flexible Master’s Option:**  
    - Allows **online study** or **on-campus attendance** as needed.  

For detailed program-specific requirements, refer to AIT's official admissions page: [AIT Admissions](https://ait.ac.th/admissions/).

question: What is the AIT English Entry Test (AIT-EET)?
gold_answer:
The Language Center (LC) offers a 90-minute in-house test of English proficiency called the AIT English Entry Test (EET). The score is based on a nine-point scale similar to the IELTS test. The Writing score, which is the most important at AIT, is based on an essay. The test result will be e-mailed within 7 days. The LC will report the test result to the AIT Admissions only if the score is satisfactory for provisional admission. If applicants fail to obtain the minimum score requirements for admission, they may take the test again.
There is no limit to the number of times they can take the test, but we encourage applicants to study and improve their English before retesting. The test is conducted several times per week on campus.
Alternatively, the test can be taken online through our online EET test application.
For more information or English test application, please see here http://languages.ait.ac.th/prospective-students/ .

**English Proficiency Requirements for Admission to Asian Institute of Technology (AIT)**

AIT requires English proficiency for admission to its postgraduate programs. Students can meet this requirement through **official test scores**, **a certificate of English medium instruction**, or the **AIT English Entrance Test (EET)**. Below are the minimum score requirements for each method:

---

### **1. Official Test Scores**
- **IELTS (Academic):**  
  - **Overall Band Score:** 6.0  
  - **Writing Band:** 6.0  
  - *Note:* Scores must be valid for **2 years** from the test date.

- **TOEFL (iBT):**  
  - **Overall Score:** 80  
  - **Writing Section:** 21–23  
  - *Note:* Scores must be valid for **2 years** from the test date.

- **TOEFL (CBT):**  
  - **Overall Score:** 213  
  - **Writing Section:** 25–26  

- **TOEFL (Paper-Based):**  
  - **Overall Score:** 550  
  - **Writing Section:** 59–61  

- **AIT English Entrance Test (EET):**  
  - **Writing Band:** 6.0  
  - *Note:* The EET is AIT’s own test, equivalent to other standardized tests. It is **not** a standardized test like IELTS or TOEFL.

---

### **2. Certificate of English Medium Instruction**
- Applicants from universities where **English is the sole medium of instruction** may submit a **certificate** signed by the university registrar.  
- **Requirement:**  
  - Submit the certificate to AIT.  
  - Upon arrival, students must take the **AIT Academic Writing Test (AWPT)** and achieve a **score of 5**.  
  - If the score is **less than 5**, the student is **not allowed to register for courses**.

---

### **3. Exemptions**
- Students from **English-speaking countries** (e.g., Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the UK, and the USA) are **exempted** from submitting English proficiency test scores.  
- Proof of citizenship must be submitted.

---

### **Additional Notes**
- **Language Support Fee:**  
  - Students who require English language support must pay a **one-time flat fee of 2,000 Baht** to cover academic English courses and workshops.  
  - This fee is **mandatory** for students who do not meet the English proficiency requirements.

- **Program-Specific Requirements:**  
  - Most programs (e.g., M-MSc-IF, PMESG, PME-GEM, PMB&F) require **one of the above English proficiency tests**.  
  - **Professional Master’s Programs** (e.g., PMESG, PME-GEM) require **at least 3 years of work experience** in relevant fields.

---

|--------------------|----------------|-------|

| **TOEFL (iBT)**     | 80 (Overall)  | Writing 21–23 |
| **TOEFL (CBT)**     | 213 (Overall) | Writing 25–26 |
| **TOEFL (Paper)**   | 550 (Overall) | Writing 59–61 |
| **AIT EET**         | 6.0 (Writing) | Institution-specific test |
| **Certificate**     | N/A           | Requires AWPT score of 5 |

---

For detailed program-specific requirements, visit AIT’s official admissions page: [AIT Admissions](https://ait.ac.th/admissions/).

question: What scholarships are offered by AIT?
gold_answer:
Royal Scholarships 
These are the most prestigious scholarships offered at AIT, providing full financial support. They are awarded to exceptional candidates with outstanding academic records.
•	His Majesty the King’s Scholarships: This scholarship covers full tuition fees, provides a stipend for living expenses, and offers a return airfare ticket. It is available for students from all Asian countries to pursue a Master's degree in any program offered by the School of Engineering and Technology (SET) or the School of Environment, Resources, and Development (SERD).
•	Her Majesty the Queen’s Scholarships: This scholarship also covers full tuition, a stipend, and airfare. It is awarded to female candidates from Asian countries to pursue a Master's degree in programs offered by SET or SERD.
Government Scholarships 
Several governments partner with AIT to offer scholarships to their citizens. The most notable one is from the Royal Thai Government.
•	Royal Thai Government (RTG) Scholarships: These scholarships are funded by the Thai government and are available for students from developing countries. They typically cover a significant portion of the tuition fees. There are different categories, including:
o	GMS (Greater Mekong Sub-region) Scholarships: For students from Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Vietnam, and Yunnan province in China.
o	ASEAN Scholarships: For students from other ASEAN member states.
AIT's Own Scholarships
AIT provides several scholarships directly from its own funds to attract talented students from around the world.
•	AIT President's Scholarships: Awarded to students with excellent academic records. This scholarship usually covers a portion of the tuition fee (often 50% to 75%).
•	AIT Fellowships: These are partial tuition scholarships awarded based on academic merit. The value of the scholarship varies.
•	Dean's Scholarships: Offered by the deans of the three schools (SET, SERD, and SOM) to outstanding applicants in their respective fields.
External and Partner Scholarships
AIT collaborates with international organizations and development agencies to offer sponsored scholarships.
•	DAAD Scholarship (German Academic Exchange Service): This scholarship is available for German students wishing to study at AIT.
•	Other Partner Scholarships: AIT often has agreements with various ministries, universities, and organizations that sponsor students to study at the institute.
Important Note: The availability of scholarships and their deadlines vary each year. It is crucial to check the official AIT admissions and scholarships website for the most current information, specific eligibility criteria, and application procedures. Typically, you apply for scholarships at the same time you submit your application for admission.

General Eligibility Criteria (applies to most AIT Scholarships)

You must normally meet the following to be considered for any scholarship at AIT:

1. Admission to an AIT Degree Program

You must first complete and submit the AIT online admission application by the relevant scholarship deadline.

You do not need to submit a separate scholarship application; once you apply for admission and indicate financial support on the application form, AIT will automatically consider you for eligible scholarships.

2. Academic Performance

Strong academic record is essential:

Most competitive scholarships, especially for Master’s or PhD, require high cumulative GPA (often ? 3.5 on a 4.0 scale for Bachelor’s degrees).

Some scholarships (e.g., Alumni Scholarship) accept GPA ? 2.75.

3. English Language Proficiency

You must meet AIT’s English requirements, typically:

IELTS Academic: Overall 6.0 with Writing 6.0,

OR AIT English Entrance Test (EET) score ? 6.0

(This requirement may vary slightly by scholarship program).

4. Supporting Documents

Commonly requested:

Academic transcripts and degree certificates

English test score

Letters of recommendation (especially for research-based or PhD scholarships)

For PhD scholarships, a research proposal is often required.

Specific Scholarship Criteria (Examples)
1. Royal Thai Government (RTG) / King’s & Queen’s Scholarships

These are among the main fully-funded scholarships:

For Master’s Programs

Outstanding undergraduate performance (GPA ? 3.5).

English proficiency per AIT requirement (IELTS/EET ? 6.0).

For Doctoral Programs

Outstanding undergraduate and Master’s performance (Bachelor’s & Master’s GPA ? 3.5).

Two recommendation letters and a research proposal.

English proficiency (IELTS/EET ? 6.0).

Coverage typically includes tuition, fees, accommodation, and a living allowance.

2. AIT Alumni Scholarship Fund (Master’s)

Any nationality is accepted.

Cumulative GPA ? 2.75.

English proficiency: IELTS Academic ? 6.0 or EET ? 6.0.

Must meet AIT admissions entry requirements.

3. DAAD Scholarship (for Select Southeast Asian Candidates)

Must be national of eligible countries (e.g., Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Malaysia, Philippines, East Timor, Thailand, Vietnam).

Completed bachelor degree within 6 years with above-average performance (often upper third of class).

Strong motivation and commitment.

English proficiency (IELTS/EET ? 6.0).

Must fulfill AIT admission requirements.

4. Other Sponsored Scholarships (e.g., Corporate Scholarships)

Some external or partner scholarships (e.g., AIS Scholarship) have specific industry criteria such as:

Nationality restrictions

Minimum GPA requirements

Relevant work experience

Technical or professional skills aligned with sponsor interest areas.

How Selection Works

Scholarships are competitive and merit-based, and applicants are automatically considered after they submit their admission form with financial support indicated.

Academic merit (GPA, research potential, English proficiency) is often the most important criterion.

Next Steps Before Applying

Check the exact scholarship deadlines for your intended intake (e.g., March 31 for Royal Thai Government scholarships).

Prepare:

Transcripts and degree certificates

English test score

Letters of recommendation

Research proposal (if required, especially for PhD)

These are merit-based awards available to students admitted to Master’s or PhD programs at AIT.

Eligible Countries:

All nationalities worldwide are eligible to apply.

This means if you are admitted and meet academic/English requirements, you can be considered for AIT central scholarships regardless of where you are from.

2. Royal Thai Government (RTG) Scholarships

These are non-bonded, fully funded scholarships provided by the Royal Thai Government for Master’s and Doctoral students.

Eligible Countries:

Any Asian nationality (for most RTG scholarships) — includes countries across Asia.

Some sub-programs (e.g., GMS / Loom Nam Khong Pijai) target specific sub-regions such as Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Vietnam, Thailand, and parts of southern China.

In general, these scholarships aim to support students from Asia broadly, with particular priority to ASEAN and other Asian countries.

3. DAAD Scholarships at AIT

Funded by the German government, these scholarships focus on specific Southeast Asian countries.

Eligible Countries for DAAD at AIT:

Cambodia

Indonesia

Lao PDR

Myanmar

Malaysia

Philippines

East Timor

Thailand

Vietnam

These are specific and not open to applicants from outside this group.

question: Are scholarships available for both Master’s and PhD students?
gold_answer: Yes. Scholarships at the Asian Institute of Technology (AIT) are available for both Master’s and PhD students. Various funding options at AIT cover postgraduate study at both degree levels — this includes AIT’s own academic scholarships as well as externally funded or partner scholarship
generated_answer:
Here’s a structured summary of the scholarships available at AIT, including eligibility criteria, study levels, and deadlines:

---

### **1. Chinese Government Scholarships**  
- **Nationality**: Chinese citizens  
- **Study Level**: Master’s and Doctoral Degree Programs  
- **Deadline**: 31 March 2026  
- **Details**: Covers tuition, accommodation, and living expenses. Requires a strong academic background and English proficiency (IELTS/AIT EET).  

---

### **2. DAAD Scholarships**  
- **Nationality**: Lao PDR, East Timor, Indonesia, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Malaysia, Philippines  
- **Study Level**: Master’s Degree Programs  
- **Deadline**: 16 February 2026  
- **Details**: Supports tuition, accommodation, and living expenses. Requires a research proposal and English proficiency.  

---

### **3. ADB-JSP Scholarships (Asian Development Bank-Japan Scholarship Program)**  
- **Nationality**: ADB borrowing member countries (e.g., Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam)  
- **Study Level**: Master’s Degree Programs  
- **Deadline**: 31 March 2026  
- **Details**: Covers tuition, accommodation, and living expenses. Requires academic excellence, English proficiency, and a return to home country after graduation.  

---

### **4. Element Solutions Foundation Scholarships**  
- **Nationality**: Laos, Philippines, Indonesia, Myanmar, Thailand, Timor Leste, Malaysia, Vietnam  
- **Study Level**: Master’s Degree Programs  
- **Deadline**: 30 November 2025  
- **Details**: Supports tuition and living expenses. Focuses on engineering, technology, and related fields.  

---

### **5. Computer and Structures, Inc. Scholarship**  
- **Nationality**: Pakistan  
- **Study Level**: Master’s Degree Programs  
- **Deadline**: 30 June 2025  
- **Details**: Covers tuition and living expenses. Open to students in engineering or technology disciplines.  

---

### **6. AIT Alumni Scholarships**  
- **Nationality**: Open to AIT alumni (no specific nationality restriction)  
- **Study Level**: Master’s Degree Programs  
- **Deadline**: 15 November 2025 (for January 2026 intake)  
- **Details**: Covers 24 credits (12 credits/semester) and registration fees for two semesters.  

---

### **7. Prof. Emeritus Madan Mohan Das Memorial Scholarship**  
- **Nationality**: Open to all (no specific restriction)  
- **Study Level**: Master’s Degree Programs  
- **Deadline**: 15 November 2025 (for January 2026 intake)  
- **Details**: Covers 24 credits and registration fees for two semesters.  

---

### **Key Notes**  
- **Flexible Master’s Option**: Available for Master’s programs. No employment proof required. Costs the same as full-time programs but offers flexible scheduling (2–4 years).  
- **Language Requirements**: Most scholarships require English proficiency (IELTS 6.0 or AIT EET).  
- **Application Process**: Submit via [AIT’s online portal](https://ait.ac.th/apply-online). Include academic transcripts, English scores, and a research proposal (for Master’s/PhD).  

For the most accurate and up-to-date information, visit [AIT’s financial aid page](https://ait.ac.th/financial-aid) or contact the **Admissions and Scholarships Unit** directly.

•	Clinic / Ambulance (Not maintenance but safety-related): ext. 5286 (Asian Institute of Technology)
•	Security / Fire / Ambulance (24 hrs): +66 2 524 6000 (ofam.ait.ac.th)
•	General AIT switchboard (main reception): +66 2 524 5000 / +66 2 524 5031-33 (Asian Institute of Technology)
3. On-campus Procedure (Typical)
1.	Phone first: Call +66 2 524 5800 during office hours for routine maintenance requests. (ofam.ait.ac.th)
2.	Emergency: Call +66 2 524 5804 after office hours. (Asian Institute of Technology)
3.	Email: Send detailed maintenance request to callcenter@ait.asia (describe issue, location, urgency, your contact info). (ofam.ait.ac.th)

•	Specify building name/room number or dorm name. (Scribd)
•	Include your contact number/email so maintenance can follow up. (Scribd)
•	For dorm repairs (student housing), you may also visit the Housing Maintenance Section in Dorm E basement during business hours. (Asian Institute of Technology)

2. How to Request Additional Cleaning
You have three main options to request cleaning services for your room or dorm unit:
A. Email Accommodation/Service Desk
•	Send your request to the Call Center email:
callcenter@ait.asia
•	In your email, include:
o	Dorm/building name and room number
o	That you want housekeeping/room cleaning
o	Your contact number
o	Preferred date/time (if any)
(For special cleaning services beyond routine weekly cleaning, these requests are processed based on availability and may include a fee.) (Facilities Management)
B. Phone Contact
•	Call the AIT Call Center / Facilities Services:
02-524-5800 (Office hours 08:00–17:00)
•	Provide your room details and request for house cleaning. (Facilities Management)
C. Facility Infrastructure Management System (FIMS)
•	Visit www.fims.ait.asia
•	Log in and submit a work request under the janitorial category for room cleaning. (Facilities Management)

Cleaning Service Pricing (Optional / Extra Service)
If you want additional cleaning services beyond the standard weekly cleaning, there are optional housekeeping service rates (charges may apply): (Facilities Management)

Official Contacts for Cleaning Requests
AIT Call Center / Facilities Help Desk
•	Phone: 02-524-5800 (office hours) (Facilities Management)
•	Email: callcenter@ait.asia (Facilities Management)
Accommodation Office (if cleaning is related to moving/room readiness)
•	Phone: 02-524-5093 (Google Sites)
•	Email: accommodation@ait.ac.th (Google Sites)
Notes
•	Routine cleaning is scheduled weekly; extra cleaning requests may be charged and are subject to staff availability. (Facilities Management)
•	Specify clearly in your request that you want room cleaning and mention whether you want standard weekly cleaning or special/deep cleaning.

question: How to Queue for CAT-2 Accommodation at AIT?
gold_answer:
At the Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), CAT-2 accommodation is allocated via a waiting list. Students must register in person using the official Google Form provided by the Accommodation Office.
Step 1: Visit the AIT Accommodation Office
•	Go physically to the Accommodation Office on campus.
•	In front of the office, you will find a QR code poster for accommodation registration.
Step 2: Scan the QR Code and Register
•	Scan the QR code using your mobile phone.
•	This opens the official Google Form for the waiting list.
•	The form may appear as “closed” when accessed externally. It typically opens only when scanned from the QR code at the office.
Step 3: Select the Correct Form
For CAT-2 accommodation, you must use:
Student Waiting List Registration Form (CAT 1, 2, 3, 4)
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1gNDZl_pZaFOo7BRvA-kIA8YbKA3__nJsR-nijZvwGG8/closedform
Other forms are for different housing types only:
•	Married Unit Waiting List
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1uRe4rtXqHwF0O4tg4lMSVLGtkeTtn59cPTFDsw-QG0Y/closedform
•	Student Village (Single) Waiting List
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1rrhGWW9Foy9FTCHZ6OENVE8iEKfxPNPSyDUJiAQG8Vo/closedform
Step 4: Complete the Form Carefully
•	Select CAT-2 as your accommodation type
•	Enter:
o	Student ID
o	Program and School
o	Contact number and email
o	Current accommodation status
Step 5: Wait for Allocation
•	After submission, your name is placed in the official CAT-2 waiting queue
•	Allocation depends on:
o	Queue order
o	Room availability
o	Student priority and eligibility
•	The Accommodation Office will contact you directly once a unit becomes available

•	Air-conditioning and balcony included

•	Private bathroom

•	Air-conditioning and balcony

•	Private bathroom
•	Full kitchen (refrigerator and gas stove)

CAT-2	Yes	Yes	Single students

Student Village – Married	Yes	Yes	Married/student families
